source.title: Solutions to four open problems on quorum colorings of graphs

accepted.question_text: Characterize the graphs G for which the quorum coloring number ψ_q(G) equals 1, and characterize the graphs G for which ψ_q(G) is greater than 1. Here a quorum coloring of a graph G is a partition of V(G) into color classes such that for every vertex v, at least half of the vertices in the closed neighborhood N[v] have the same color as v; ψ_q(G) is the maximum number of color classes in such a coloring.
accepted.context_brief: Characterization of graphs by quorum coloring number

evidence.quote: Can you characterize the class of graphs for which ψq(G) = 1 or the class of graphs for which ψq(G) > 1?

In this paper, we give answers to four open problems stated in 2013 by Hedetniemi, Hedetniemi, Laskar and Mulder. In particular, we show that there is no good characterization of the graphs G with ψq(G) = 1 nor for those with ψq(G) > 1 unlessP̸ =NP∩ co−NP .

accepted.question_text: Find an infinite family of graphs, other than the odd complete graphs K_(2n+1) and the joins K_r + K_s with r + s odd and r ≥ 2, for which the quorum coloring number ψ_q(G) equals 1.

evidence.quote: In fact, can you ﬁnd any inﬁnite family of graphs other than those of the form K2n+1 or Kr + Ks for r + s odd and r≥ 2, for which ψq(G) = 1?

In this paper, we answer Questions 1, 2, 3 and 4 as follows. In Sections 2 and 3 we give a ﬁrst and a second answer to Question 1, respectively. In Section 4, we give a third answer to Question 1 which also answers Question 2 in negative, and in Section 5 we give a fourth answer to Question 1

accepted.question_text: Is the condition ψ_q(G) = 1 equivalent to the conjunction that the defensive alliance number a(G) equals ⌈n/2⌉ and the order n = |V(G)| is odd? Here a defensive alliance is a subset S of V(G) such that every v in S has at least as many vertices of N[v] inside S as outside S.
accepted.context_brief: Relation between ψ_q(G) and defensive alliance number

evidence.quote: Is ψq(G) = 1 if and only if a(G) =⌈n/2⌉ and n is odd?
which therefore answers also Question 2 in negative.

accepted.question_text: If a graph G satisfies ψ_q(G) = 1, must its diameter diam(G) be at most 2?

evidence.quote: Hence, we deduce that lim ℓ→+∞ diam(Gℓ) = +∞, which answers Questions 3 and 4 in negative.

accepted.question_text: Does every graph G satisfy the inequality ⌊diam(G)/2⌋ ≤ ψ_q(G), where diam(G) is the graph diameter and ψ_q(G) is the quorum coloring number?

evidence.quote: Hence, we deduce that lim ℓ→+∞ diam(Gℓ) = +∞, which answers Questions 3 and 4 in negative.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the family of join graphs K_r + G for which ψ_q(K_r + G) = 1, where K_r is the complete graph on r vertices and K_r + G denotes the join obtained by adding all edges between K_r and G.

evidence.quote: 1. Characterize the family of graphs Kr + G for which ψq(Kr + G) = 1.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the family of join graphs G + H for which ψ_q(G + H) = 1, where G + H is the join of two graphs obtained from their disjoint union by adding every edge between a vertex of G and a vertex of H.

evidence.quote: 2. Characterize the family of graphs G + H for which ψq(G + H) = 1.

accepted.question_text: Find complete multipartite graphs G, other than the family described in Corollary 4.2, such that ψ_q(G) = 1.

evidence.quote: 3. Can you ﬁnd complete multipartite graphs G other than those of Corollary 4.2 such that ψq(G) = 1?

accepted.question_text: Characterize the graphs G with diameter exactly 2 for which the quorum coloring number ψ_q(G) equals 1.

evidence.quote: 4. Characterize the class of graphs G, with diam(G) = 2 for which ψq(G) = 1.

accepted.question_text: Characterize the graphs G for which the inequality ⌊diam(G)/2⌋ ≤ ψ_q(G) holds.
